title: The Small Postcards
premise: Ivo Nystrom, once a celebrated composer who abandoned music after a betrayal he has never explained, works as a janitor at the conservatory where he was a prodigy. When a radio broadcasts a song he knows was written by his late friend Lena and never recorded, he realizes someone is claiming her work — and that the man responsible is now a powerful conductor preparing a career-defining premiere. Returning to the northern town where their story went wrong, Ivo uncovers letters, postcards, and witnesses that prove the theft, but must choose between public justice and protecting the living people entangled in the lie. In the end, he performs Lena's song himself at the premiere's intermission, surrendering his anonymity and his safety to return her name to the world.
about_author: M. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former conservatory librarian who spent fifteen years cataloguing unpublished manuscripts before turning to fiction. They write quietly devastating novels about art, memory, and the debts we owe the dead.

chapters.title: The Tenant
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. We meet him mopping the conservatory corridors at dawn, invisible among students who don't know he once premiered here at seventeen. A routine of deliberate smallness: he touches no piano, answers no questions about his past. The emotional beat is self-erasure — a man who has made invisibility into a discipline, waiting for nothing.

chapters.title: A Song on the Radio
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In a diner, a radio plays 'The Small Postcards' — a melody Lena wrote the winter she died, never recorded, never published. He drops his coffee; the waitress thinks he's ill. The broadcast credits a rising conductor, Emil Varga. The emotional beat is vertigo: the past reaching through the static to claim him.

chapters.title: What Lena Left
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, with flashbacks. He opens the box he swore never to open: her handwritten score, postcards she sent him from the north, each one unfinished. Flashbacks reveal their friendship and the night everything broke — the fire, the accusation, his silence. The beat is grief sharpening into resolve: he will go back.

chapters.title: Northbound
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV on the train north, intercut with a young conductor's memory of Varga as a hungry student. He arrives in the fading coastal town where they studied together, finding the old academy half-abandoned. The beat is dread mixed with homecoming — every street accuses him of having stayed away so long.

chapters.title: The Widow's Door
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Ivo and Marta, Lena's older sister, who has kept the house like a shrine. Marta recognizes him instantly and slams the door — she blames Ivo for Lena's death. But a neighbor mentions Varga visited last month, buying silence. The beat is hostility cracking into shared suspicion.

chapters.title: Postcards, Unsent
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. She shows Ivo a bundle of postcards Lena never sent — including one naming Varga as the man taking her work, dated days before her death. Marta reveals Lena didn't die by accident; she walked onto the ice road. The beat is terrible intimacy: two keepers of the same wound finally comparing scars.

chapters.title: Varga's Premiere
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He confronts Varga at rehearsal in the city concert hall; Varga is charming, then chillingly honest — the world needs the music more than it needs the truth, and Ivo's own silence made him complicit. Varga offers him money and co-credit. The beat is seduction and disgust: the offer is almost reasonable, which is what makes it monstrous.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Waited
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Ivo and old caretaker Henrik, the only witness to Lena's final night. Henrik, dying, gives Ivo her lost notebook and confesses he stayed silent for thirty years out of fear. Rising tension: Varga learns Ivo has evidence and threatens to expose Ivo's own role in the fire. The beat is the trap closing.

chapters.title: Intermission
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, climax. At the premiere, during intermission, Ivo walks onstage uninvited and plays 'The Small Postcards' from Lena's manuscript, telling the hall whose hands wrote it. Uproar; security moves; Varga freezes as the audience recognizes the melody already billed as his. The beat is terror transfigured into release — Ivo finally owns the stage by giving it away.

chapters.title: Owner of Nothing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Ivo and Marta, epilogue. The scandal unravels Varga's career; Ivo faces consequences but refuses credit beyond restoring Lena's name. He returns north, and Marta finally lets him into the house — into Lena's room. He mails the unsent postcards, one by one, to no address. The beat is quiet restitution: a tenant no longer, an owner of nothing but the truth.
